note: Bluebonnet's shape sections for the shape loop tools (docs/jclass-1 to docs/jclass-9). "Hull" is slice 1's moulded hull, kept as the measured reference: it is in no section, so render_set.py hides it, and slice 2's painted shell (the same surface, cut at its paint lines, the lead's top and the rudder) is what renders. The rudder and its stock are their own objects, placed by a frame that turns about the stock line (build.json finish.rudder.frame); so is the wheel, in a frame whose X runs forward along its shaft (build.json deck.wheel_frame). Slice 3's deck closes the shell at the sheer and the transom's top. Slice 4's spars are three objects: the mast with everything fixed to it (spreaders, jumper struts, tracks, bands, the gooseneck's lug and pin, the pole's car), and the boom and the spinnaker pole, each in a frame that turns about its pin (build.json rig.boom_frame and rig.pole_frame). Slice 5's rigging is the shrouds and the stays (two objects, with their tangs, sockets, rigging screws and chainplates), the runners' and checkstays' tangs and padeyes, and each runner and checkstay in two states, Set and LetOff (Runner.<Side>.<State>, Checkstay.<Side>.<State>): the build shows the starboard-tack pair (starboard set, port let off) and hides the others. Slice 6's sails are one object per sail and state (Mainsail.Set, Mainsail.Run, Mainsail.Lowered, Mainsail.Flaked, Mainsail.Stack; Genoa, Quadrilateral and Staysail .Set, .Lowered, .Bagged; Spinnaker.Set, Spinnaker.Bagged): the mainsail's Lowered and Flaked lie in the boom's frame (each carries it as its 'frame'), the rest in the hull's. The build shows the genoa's suit (Mainsail.Set and Genoa.Set) and hides the others; build.json sails.suits lists which states are set together. Slice 7's running rigging is the winches with their pads and cleats (Winches), the lead blocks' padeyes and the halyards' boxes on the mast with each halyard's lead from its foot box to its reel (RunningFittings), and one object per suit (Running.<Suit>: the ropes, blocks and shackles as that suit leads them); the build shows Running.Genoa and hides the others. Slice 8's deck hardware is the fixed pieces (DeckHardware: the stem head, mooring cleats and fairleads, the cowls' flanges, deck prisms, the anchor on its chocks, the chain pipe, the side and stern lights and the ensign's socket; the sheet tracks are RunningFittings'), the cowls standing in harbour (Cowls.Moored) and their flanges' caps at sea (CowlCaps.<Suit> for the other suits), the ensign on its staff flown in harbour (Ensign.Moored) and one burgee per suit (Burgee.<Suit>, streaming down that suit's apparent wind); the build shows Burgee.Genoa and CowlCaps.Genoa and hides the others. Slice 9's interior forward is five objects, loaded only when the camera is below (each carries 'slice' 9): the steel and the deckhead (Below.Structure: the plating's inside, frames, beams, knees, carlins and the headers across the openings' ends, the mast partners, the forward bulkhead's steel plate, the deckhead's painted planking under the deck), the ceiling (Below.Ceiling: the battens, and the galley's painted tongue-and-groove lining; the forepeak is bare), the joiner's work (Below.Joinery: bulkheads and doors, soles and steps, ladders, the galley's counter, dresser, lockers and ice chest, the mess, the sail bins, the washroom's woodwork, the chain locker, the forepeak's platform, the windlass's bed, the bower's chocks and the bosun's shelves), the metal fittings (Below.Fittings: the cots' pipe frames and their hooks and chains, the range, the sink, the pump, the WC and basin, the windlass, the cable, the bower, the spurling and navel pipes) and the canvas (Below.Canvas: the cots' canvas and lacing, the sail bags); the bow chock on deck is DeckHardware's. The game streams the five in together, when the camera goes below (build.json triangles_slice_9_objects).
